ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the decision-framing, vivid failure modes (a system that works 80% of the time but fails when it matters, wasted development time, frustrated users), the 2024-2025 startup-stakes claim, and the framework preview.

Understanding the Spectrum: From Workflows to Agents:
**1:** Both sections cover the workflow/agent definitions, characteristics, and analogies, and the future-concept callouts (chaining/routing/orchestrator-worker; tools/memory/ReAct, all named). The added historical rule-based-systems context is additive and doesn't affect completeness.

Choosing Your Path:
**1:** Both sections cover the control-framing trade-off, workflow/agent strengths and weaknesses, the hybrid/autonomy-slider discussion with Cursor and Perplexity, and this is one of the few articles to include the 'deleted codebase' joke. The added 'sobering reality of production adoption' point is additive.

Exploring Common Patterns:
**0:** Chaining/routing, orchestrator-worker, and evaluator-optimizer are all present and match. The ReAct components explicitly compare short-term memory to RAM (matching the expected section's own analogy), but long-term memory is only named, with no analogy or explanation of its specific function (access to factual knowledge, remembering user preferences) at all -- weaker treatment of long-term memory than several other articles reviewed, since even the diagram-only or hard-drive-analogy attempts seen elsewhere are absent here.

Zooming In on Our Favorite Examples:
**0:** The Gemini CLI and Perplexity examples are covered, each with a genuine bonus addition (see depth/breadth below). However, the expected section's Gemini CLI use-case enumeration and 'Similar tools' list are both absent, as in most articles reviewed.

The Challenges of Every AI Engineer:
**1:** Both sections cover all five challenges (with genuine bonus specificity on reliability and security, see depth below), the 'solvable' point, and the path-forward closing, which correctly names 'structured outputs' as next lesson's topic.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose. One notable issue for transparency: reference [21] attributes the arXiv paper at https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25423v2 to 'Penedo, A., et al. (2025), AI Agent Development: An Evidence-based Technical Analysis of Challenges, Patterns, and Lessons Learned' -- but that URL's actual content in research.md (verified across multiple presets in this session) is a different paper, 'What Challenges Do Developers Face in AI Agent Systems? An Empirical Study on Stack Overflow & GitHub Issues' by Asgari, Panichella, Derakhshanfar, and Olsthoorn. The title and authors appear fabricated even though the URL and the underlying claims drawn from it are real; this doesn't change this criterion's score but is flagged here as a verifiable citation fabrication.
